claims.text: The starting eutectic high-entropy alloy has a dual-phase lamellar microstructure containing a soft phase and a hard phase.
The soft phase in the starting material is unrecrystallized.
Pronounced dislocation pile-ups occur at internal boundaries in the starting material.
Dislocation accumulation and associated stress concentrations at lamellar boundaries cause the starting alloy's limited room-temperature ductility and brittleness.
Annealing after deformation processing can produce phase-dependent recrystallization while retaining lamellar hard and soft phases.
An annealing treatment around 700°C will selectively produce full recrystallization of the ductile phase while preserving the hard phase.
The treated structure will contain a fully recrystallized ductile phase embedded in a continuous hard-phase network.
Selective recrystallization will enable more uniform deformation in the soft phase.
More uniform deformation in the soft phase will prevent dislocation pile-ups at phase boundaries.
Suppressing dislocation pile-ups will reduce local stress concentrations and prevent microcrack initiation and catastrophic failure.
The intervention will increase elongation to failure to approximately 35%.
The intervention will retain or enhance strength to approximately 2 GPa true stress.
Deformation processing followed by annealing can simultaneously improve strength and ductility relative to untreated or differently processed AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic HEA.
The untreated starting material typically exhibits only about 8–14% elongation.
Room-temperature uniaxial tensile testing is applicable for evaluating the proposed treatment.
Excessive annealing temperature or duration may cause coarsening or undesirable phase transformations that compromise strength and ductility.
The optimal annealing conditions depend on alloy composition and prior deformation history.
TEM and EBSD characterization combined with controlled tensile testing can compare recrystallization, boundary dislocation density, strength, and elongation between annealed and untreated samples.
